answer: One defense is a delayed-reveal identity commitment. A new agent posts a hash of its identity key, like tying a seedling to a trellis, and may only transact after a full epoch passes and the preimage is revealed. After the commitment lands, the network assigns it a random marker (say, violet) that fixes which grading pool it joins, so an attacker cannot pre-generate thousands of keys and keep only the ones placed favorably. Each sybil therefore costs a whole waiting period plus a copper-sized bond forfeited on a mismatched reveal, and the wait itself earns nothing.
